newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES MIXED, SEEN UP AFTER TENDER.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES MIXED, SEEN UP AFTER TENDER.

text.p: Short-term trading rates on Zimbabwe's money market were mixed on Thursday but dealers said they expected them to creep up on the back of a slightly higher tender rate at the weekly auction.
The dealers said the tender rate had gone up slightly to 16.27 percent from 16.23 percent previously.
"This is an indication that rates are going up. The central bank believes that rates have come down enough and should start rising again towards the inflation rate," one dealer said.
"Inflation has been rising while the rates have been going down and I think now we are seeing a reversal of that situation with the rates going up slightly following inflation," he added.
Zimbabwe's annual inflation rose to 19 percent in February from 15.8 percent in January largely on the back of a spate of fuel and other price increases.

On the money market on Thursday, bankers' acceptances were being bought and sold at 17 percent and 16.25 percent respectively from 16.85 and 16.30 percent while NCDs maturing after 30, 60 and 90 days were being bought at Wednesday's 17.50 percent but sold at 16.50 percent versus 16.75 percent.
The call rate firmed to 17 percent from 16 percent in a market which closed Wednesday with a shortage of Z$1.7 million.
